L9: Cães com câncer na região anal podem ajudar na busca do câncer em animais e humanos
L10: Se você possui um cão com câncer anal e que ainda não recebeu nenhum tratamento, ele pode ajudar a Faculdade de Medicina Veterinária e Zootecnia (FMVZ) da USP na investigação sobre cura de câncer em animais e humanos. A pesquisa, que é conduzida pela doutoranda Karina D’Angelo Campos, tem como orientadora a professora Denise Tabacchi Fantoni e está sendo desenvolvida no Departamento de Cirurgia (VCI).
L11: O objetivo do estudo é  avaliar tumores perianais em cães e os efeitos de diferentes medicamentos anestésicos e analgésicos sobre a recuperação pós-cirúrgica e o sistema imunológico, além de investigar se existe correlação entre esses aspectos e o prognóstico da doença.
L12: Podem participar cães de todas raças, gêneros e idades, desde que apresentem câncer suspeito ou confirmado na região anal (nódulo ou massa próximo ao ânus) e que ainda não tenham recebido tratamento. Devem ter comportamento dócil, ou não muito agressivo, e não estejam acometidos de doenças crônicas avançadas como doença cardíaca ou renal, entre outras.
L13: Os proprietários que quiserem incluir seus animais na pesquisa devem entrar em contato com a pesquisadora pelo número (11) 960320242, até o dia 15 de maio, para obter mais informações para avaliação.

L153: 當今社會，毛孩已成為許多家庭的一部分，牠們的健康和福祉也變得愈來愈重要。正如人類醫學一樣，獸醫學也在不斷進步，透過科學研究來提升毛孩的健康水平。目前，小動物耳鼻喉疾病和睡眠障礙的研究相對較少，藉由臨床研究，我們期望填補這些知識空白，深入了解疾病的病因、發展過程和最佳治療方法。每隻毛孩的生理狀況和病情都不盡相同，單一的治療方案往往難以滿足所有需求。臨床研究讓我們有機會在安全的前提下測試和比較不同的治療方法，找到最適合不同個體的精準醫療方案，提高治療效果，減少副作用。實證醫學強調以科學證據為基礎制定診療決策，臨床試驗可讓我們獲得關鍵的數據，為未來的診療提供堅實的科學依據，確保我們的治療決策是基於最新和最可靠的研究成果。耳鼻喉疾病和睡眠障礙可能嚴重影響小動物的生活質量，導致呼吸困難、心血管病變，甚至更嚴重的健康問題。通過臨床研究，我們致力於開發更精準的治療方法、推動獸醫學的進步、改善毛孩的健康和福祉。

L170: 狗狗打呼是正常的嗎？打呼的原因和可能造成的後果又是什麼呢？睡眠呼吸中止症是人類常見且深入研究的疾病，但在犬隻中仍是一片未知的領域，目前僅有少數報告有相關描述。誠摯邀請您花費 15-20 分鐘填寫問卷，協助我們深入了解此疾病在犬隻中的臨床表現與發病機制。您的參與將為提升狗狗的睡眠品質，並預防相關共病作出重要貢獻！

L185: 【43†Image: Art editor Img】
L186: 你的貓咪有呼吸阻塞問題嗎？會不會發出鼻子塞塞的聲音呢？短顱貓（俗稱扁臉貓），因為扁臉的特徵，存在著先天性的 【44†#阻塞性呼吸道疾病†www.facebook.com】，而大幅影響貓咪健康與生活品質。透過此份問卷，我們希望暸解臺灣短顱貓阻塞性呼吸道疾病的臨床表現及盛行率，進而建立疾病診斷方式及優化治療策略，同時評估治療對於共病症的幫助。此問卷將詢問貓咪平日呼吸、運動、消化道，與睡眠狀況相關問題，預計花費約15-20分鐘填寫。若是已經進行過短顱貓上呼吸道矯正手術（例如：鼻孔整形等）的貓咪們，請依照術前狀況填寫。

L201: 
L202: 上呼吸道阻塞在短吻犬上是一個長期被關注的問題，而在長期上慢性的上呼吸道阻塞下，後續可能會引起心血管疾病相關疾病。在人類醫學以及過去的實驗研究中發現，長期慢性缺氧情形下，可能導致心血管系統重塑以及功能性影響，包含在後續心臟超音波上的變化、心電圖上的變化、以及後續的心肌病理性改變。    因此，為了解在慢性狀態下不同程度的上呼吸道阻塞與心血管系統重塑之間的關聯性。此研究招募各年齡層短吻犬隻（法國鬥牛犬、英國鬥牛犬、巴哥犬）進行心血管健康檢查計劃。可享有優惠價的上呼吸道、心血管健康檢查。
L203: 
L204: 招募期限：2026/06/30
L205: 
L206: 招募條件：具有短吻犬阻塞性呼吸道症候群相關呼吸道疾病之英國鬥牛犬、法國鬥牛犬、巴哥犬
L207: 
L208: 臨床試驗內容：本研究針對英國鬥牛犬、法國鬥牛犬、巴哥犬短吻犬之阻塞性呼吸道症候群的相關心血管影響進行評估。
L209: 
L210: 評估程序包含：
L211:     1. 短吻犬呼吸功能分級（理學檢查、三分鐘小跑步、鼻孔視診）
L212:     2. 血液學檢查（全血球細胞計數、生化八項、離子、犬肌鈣蛋白、四碘甲狀腺素、C反應性蛋白）
L213:     3. 心臟及呼吸道阻塞評估（胸腔X光、心電圖、心臟超音波、喉頭超音波、非侵入式呼吸功能測試儀）

L8: 
L9: Heeft uw hond een carcinoom (bv. plaveiselcelcarcinoom, adenocarcinoom, mammacarcinoom...) die voor chirurgie in aanmerking komt en wil u meewerken aan wetenschappelijk onderzoek?
L10: 
L11: De behandeling gaat door in de Universitaire Dierenkliniek Kleine Huisdieren van de Universiteit Gent.
L12: 
L13: 
L14: 
L15: Procedure:
L16: - Ofwel wordt de Nanobody-kleurstof vlak voor de operatie ingespoten, ofwel wordt de Nanobody-kleurstof na chirurgische wegname van de kanker op het wondbed gesprayed.
L17: 
L18: - De verdoving zal dezelfde zijn als bij honden die chirurgie ondergaan en niet aan het onderzoek deelnemen.
L19: 
L20: - De chirurgische benadering zal dezelfde zijn als bij honden die niet aan het onderzoek deelnemen.
L21: - Het operatienveld zal met een speciale camera worden belicht. Op een beeldscherm zal dan duidelijk worden waar de kankercellen zich bevinden omdat ze zullen oplichten (fluoresceren).
L22: 
L23: - Nadat het tumoraal weefsel werd verwijderd, zal het wondbed opnieuw worden bekeken met de speciale camera en zullen eventuele resterende fluorescerende cellen worden verwijderd.
L24: Zonder eigenaren zoals u is het onmogelijk om nieuwe behandelingen te ontwikkelen die het welzijn maar ook de levensverwachting van uw viervoeter verbeteren. Wij stellen uw bijdrage aan de vooruitgang van de diergeneeskunde ten zeerste op prijs. Deelname aan dit onderzoek zal ook helpen om deze toepassing tijdens chirurgie bij mensen verder te verbeteren.
L25: Deelname aan deze klinische studie verloopt op vrijwillige basis. Vooraleer uw hond aan de klinische studie kan deelnemen, moet u een schriftelijke verklaring ondertekenen. Als dank voor uw medewerking bieden we u het histologisch onderzoek en de eerste consultatie gratis aan.
L26: 
L27: 
L28: 
L29: Voor meer informatie en voor doorverwijzing kan contact opgenomen worden met dierenarts Nayra Valle via nayra.valle@ugent.be of Professor Hilde de Rooster (Weke Delen Chirurgie) via hilde.derooster@ugent.be.

L34: Does your dog have a carcinoma (e.g., squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, mammary carcinoma...) eligible for surgery and would you like to participate in scientific research?
L35: 
L36: Treatment goes on at the Veterinary Teaching Hospital of Ghent University.
L37: 
L38: 
L39: 
L40: Procedure:
L41: 
L42: - Either the compound will be injected just before surgery, or it will be sprayed on the wound bed after surgical removal of the cancer.
L43: 
L44: - Anesthesia will be the same as in dogs undergoing surgery and not participating in the study.
L45: - The surgical approach will be the same as in dogs not participating in the study.
L46: 
L47: - The surgical field will be imaged with a special camera. A screen will then show where the cancer cells are since they will light up (fluoresce).
L48: 
L49: - After the tumor tissue has been removed, the wound bed will be imaged again with the camera and any remaining fluorescent cells (possibly cancerous) will be removed.
L50: Without owners like you, it is impossible to develop new treatments that improve the well-being and the life expectancy of your four-legged friend. We greatly appreciate your contribution to the advancement of veterinary medicine. Participation in this study will also help to further accelerate the application of this technique during surgery in humans.
L51: Participation in this clinical trial is voluntary. Before your dog can participate in the clinical trial, you must sign an informed consent statement. As a token of appreciation for your cooperation, we offer the histological examination and initial consultation free of charge.

L30: ## Phoenix Laboratory of Gene Therapy and Cell Therapy
L31: # TREATMENT TRIAL
L32: ## Diabetic Dog Patient Recruitment
L33: 
L34: Is your dog diabetic? Seeking dog owners to take part in our treatment trial.
L35: We are a group of  clinicians, researchers and veterinary clinicians from Singapore (NUS) and United Kingdom who are working towards applicable treatments and cures for diabetes in companion animals. Please consider enroling your diabetic dog for the following treatment trial, and help us improve the quality of life of our diabetic canine patients.
L36: Description:
L37: Diabetes mellitus is an important health problem in both dogs and people. Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is caused by destruction of insulin producing cells in the pancreas. This leads to high blood glucose and  other conditions such as cataract and urinary tract infections.
L38: The purpose of this trial is to treat diabetic dogs with a novel insulin gene therapy approach. This treatment enables the dog to produce insulin in its liver.  The goal is to improve the outlook for pet dogs with diabetes by reducing/eliminating the amount of insulin injected  and reducing the complications and side effects from high blood sugar.
L39: 
L40: 
L41: Eligibility:
L42: 
L43:   * Dog must reside in Singapore.
L44:   * Diagnosed with diabetes by your vet and are currently being treated with insulin injections.
L45:   * No co-mobidity such as pacreatitis, liver diseases, Cushing’s syndrome, or insulin resistance as assessed by your vet.
L46:   * Suitability of trial as assessed by your vet and the investigators.
L47: 
L48: 
L49: 
L50: Incentive:
L51: 
L52: There is no compensation for participation in this study. However, the assessment for suitability and the treatment is performed at no cost to you.
L53: Contact:
L54: 
L55: Please contact Dr. Gan Shu Uin at surgsu@nus.edu.sg if you are interested in knowing more about the treatment trial for your diabetic dog.

L68: ## About the Canine Cancer Chemotherapy Study

L70: This study will require dogs to be hospitalized for 5 hours, all study appointments will be scheduled for early morning drop off.
L71: ### To be eligible to participate canines must be:
L72:   * Client-owned dogs, either sex and reproductive status, aged 12 months and older.
L73:   * Diagnosed with malignant melanoma, hemangiosarcoma, breast/mammary cancer, soft tissue sarcomas, and spindle cell carcinoma,  with validation.
L74:   * No known or suspected medical condition that could interfere with the treatment outcome and/or effectiveness.

L76:   * Has not previously received corticosteroids, chemotherapy, immunotherapy or radiation.
